transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess work sent me. At the warehouse I’ve been doing stuff they don’t like—like stopping near the forklift with my arms up, making the beeping sounds, copying the hand signals. Sometimes I move boxes around in… patterns, I guess. People yell at me to stop.
Before you do those things at work, do you get an unwanted thought or feeling that you have to make it come out just right?
I don’t know. I don’t really think of it like… a thought I have to fix. It just kind of happens, I guess.
Right before you do those movements or sounds, do you feel a build-up or pressure inside that goes away once you do them?

Not really like pressure, no. I just end up doing it… like stopping there with my arms up, or making the beeps and copying the hand signals. Or the boxes, putting them in those patterns. Even when people are telling me to cut it out.
When you do those movements or sounds at work, is it because a voice or something other people can’t hear is telling you to do them?
I… I don’t know. I don’t really think of it like that. It’s not like I’m trying to listen to somebody, I just… do it.
Do you get upset when things are not arranged the way you expect them to be?
Not really… I mean, I notice stuff sometimes, but I don’t think I get upset about it like that. I’m not sure.
When you do those beeping sounds or copy the hand signals, does it feel enjoyable or interesting to you?
No… I don’t think it’s enjoyable. It’s just what happens. Like the beeping or copying the signals, or moving the boxes around that way… people yell at me to stop, but I still end up doing it.
Growing up, was it hard for you to understand other people or make friends?
I don’t know… I guess I was kind of quiet. I don’t really remember it being, like, a big thing. Friends were… some, I guess. Not a lot.
Has anyone told you that your behavior seems odd or hard to understand even when you’re not doing the beeping or copying at work?

I mean… yeah, I guess people say I’m acting weird. Mostly at the warehouse. They say I’ll just stand there with my arms up near the forklift, or start copying the beeps and hand signals, or move boxes around in these little patterns. I don’t really know how to explain it. They yell at me to stop and I still… do it.
When you start copying the forklift beeps or hand signals, do you know it’s unusual while you’re doing it?

Not really… not while it’s happening. I guess after, when people are yelling, I can tell they think it’s strange. But in the moment I’m just… doing the beeps or the hand signals, or standing there like that. I don’t think it through.
When this happens, does it feel like something outside you is controlling your body?
I don’t know. It doesn’t really feel like… something outside, I guess. It just kind of happens. I’m not thinking about it that way.
Do you often have trouble understanding what other people mean, like jokes or hints?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I don’t really pay attention to jokes and stuff. People laugh and I just kind of… wait. I’m not sure what you mean by hints.
When you move the boxes into patterns, does that feel calming to you?
Maybe. I don’t know if calming is the word. I just… move them into little patterns sometimes at the warehouse, even if people are telling me to stop. It feels like I’m supposed to keep doing it.
Do people tell you that the way you talk is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?

Yeah… sometimes. Like at work, my supervisor asks which pallets go on the truck, and I try to answer, but then I’m talking about the load sheet and… other stuff, like my old house or fishing or church boxes. Then people just look at me like they don’t know what I’m saying.
Do you believe something is going on that other people say is not true?
I don’t know. People say a lot of things. I guess sometimes I think something’s off, but… I don’t really want to get into it.
Do you feel that people at work are trying to harm you?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say harm me. I just keep to myself. I don’t really know what they’re thinking.
Do you believe someone is monitoring you at work?
I’m not sure. I mean… I haven’t really caught anyone doing that. I just try to do my work and not pay too much attention.
Do you ever hear voices when no one is there?
I don’t know… not really. Sometimes I hear things, but I’m not sure if it’s like… voices or just noise.
Do you believe something is happening around you that other people say isn’t true?
I don’t know. I guess… maybe sometimes things feel off, but I can’t really say it’s something happening. People usually say I’m overthinking, so… I just leave it alone.
Do you believe the forklift beeps or hand signals are sending you a special message meant for you?
I don’t think so. I mean, the beeps are just… work stuff, right? I haven’t really noticed any message in them.
When you start answering a question, do your thoughts sometimes drift off so that you end up talking about things that aren’t related to what was asked?

Yeah… I guess that happens. Like at work, if my supervisor asks which pallets go on the truck, I try to answer, but then I start talking about the load sheet and somehow it goes to my old house, or fishing, or church boxes… and then people just look at me like they don’t know what I’m saying.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with a schizophrenia-spectrum psychotic disorder, best coded here as schizophrenia, unspecified. The patient shows markedly disorganized behavior (posturing near the forklift, repetitive imitation of beeps/hand signals, arranging boxes into patterns despite consequences), impaired insight into the oddity of the behavior in the moment, and disorganized thought/speech with tangential answers that become difficult to follow. OCD is less likely because there are no clearly described intrusive obsessions, anxiety relief, or intact insight around compulsions. Tourette syndrome is less likely because the behaviors are not described as simple motor/vocal tics with premonitory urge relief, but rather as more complex, context-bound disorganized/imitative behavior. Asperger syndrome is less likely because developmental social-communication history is insufficient and does not explain the apparent thought disorganization and psychotic-spectrum features.
